To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the presence of nanofillers has a positive influence on the flame retardancy of polyurethane foamed materials, which was confirmed during the tests conducted using a cone calorimetric and smoke-generating apparatus.

the use of nanofillers, in particular multi-walled carbon tubes, in rigid polyurethane foam modified with halogen-free flame retarded systems, significantly improves the flame retardancy properties of the material.
the addition of halogen-free flame-retardant systems containing nanofillers significantly improves the flame retardancy of polyurethane foamed plastics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new fire retardants based on halogen-free flame-retardant systems and nanofillings for rigid polyurethane foam, which will be used in the automotive industry and construction.
the analysis of the flammability of rigid polyurethanes containing halogen-free fire-retardants, which may find use in various fields of the automotive industry.
the development of fire retardant systems for polyurethane foaming agents, which may find application in the production of rigid polyurethanes for the construction industry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of the developed flame retardant systems in the form of nanocomposites allows for the production of polyurethane foamed materials with a significantly improved fire safety.

the use of the developed flame retardants and nanoadditives in the form of carbon nanotubes and titanium dioxide allows for the production of polyurethane foam materials with reduced flammability and reduced smoke emission.
the developed flame retardant systems are promising and may be considered as the basis for further development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the developed fire retardant system based on the use of multi-walled CNTs or nano-TiO2 and halogen-free FRs can be recommended for application as a flame retardant additive to polyurethane foamed products.
the use of halogen-free flame-retardant systems containing nanoadditives can lead to the development of new, more effective fire-resistant polyurethane materials.

the use of the developed halogen-free fire retarded systems, containing nanofillers, allows for the production of polyurethane foamed plastics with a high level of flammability protection, which is comparable with the level of protection provided by halogen-based fire retardant systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of halogen-free flame-retardants in conjunction with carbon nanofillers can significantly improve the fire performance of polyurethane foaming products.
the use of nanofillers as a part of the fire-retarding system can significantly reduce the amount of halogenated flame retardants used in polyurethane foaming.
the use of nanofillers is an effective method of increasing the fire retardancy of polyurethane foamed materials.
